formulations.text: Let (X,d_X) and (Y,d_Y) be metric spaces and f:X→Y. The map f is globally Lipschitz on X if there exists L≥0 such that d_Y(f(x),f(y))≤L d_X(x,y) for every x,y∈X.

context: Mutual independence of a sequence of measurable-space-valued random variables
editorial_screening_reason: ProofWiki defines a sequence of random variables taking values in one measurable space as independent precisely when their generated σ-algebras are mutually independent. The generated σ-algebra is X_n^{-1}(S), i.e. the collection of preimages of all measurable subsets of S, not the single preimage of the whole target S. The notation (S,Σ_S) explicitly distinguishes the target underlying set and its σ-algebra, and the generated σ-algebra formula quantifies over all B∈Σ_S. This is joint/mutual independence of all finite distinct subcollections, NOT merely pairwise independence, and does not require that the X_n are real-valued. Its prerequisites can be checked against independently screened random-variable, probability-space and independent-σ-algebra meanings after source intake. Independence is mutual independence of generated sub-sigma-algebras, not pairwise independence.

formulations.text: Let (Ω,F,P) be a probability space, (S,Σ_S) a measurable target space, and X_n:Ω→S measurable for each n. The sequence (X_n) is mutually independent if the σ-algebras σ(X_n)={X_n⁻¹(B):B∈Σ_S} form a mutually independent sequence of sub-σ-algebras of F.
